rows.t: Logo design is covered by the standard Desktop license; outlines may be converted to paths. A logo used as the primary design element on merchandise for sale requires a Merchandise license.
Signage is part of the Desktop license. Video and broadcast need only a Desktop license for the production workstations, with no extra fees.

Sharing desktop fonts with subcontractors requires a Distribution add-on, counted by the number of third parties working simultaneously. Temporary staff and contractors working expressly for the licensee are covered.
No format conversion, added or deleted characters, spacing or kerning changes, or reverse engineering without written permission. Webfont subsetting is the only permitted modification.
Use of the fonts with generative or other AI services, or in AI programming, is expressly prohibited.

blocks.title: Discounts & Trials
blocks.lead: Free trial fonts with a limited Latin character set — no student discount on full licenses.

rows.t: Free, Latin-only character set, valid email required. For private use only: self-evaluation, client approval, and student projects. Full character sets can be tested on request.
rows.sub: Any public-facing work, including student work for clients, requires a paid license.

rows.t: No student discount on full licenses; students can use the trial fonts for student projects. Educational institutions can ask about site licenses.
Fonts can be rented monthly via Fontstand. Buying several families of a collection at once earns a discount of $50 per additional family, multiplied by license terms.

blocks.title: Pricing Model
blocks.lead: Every license type has its own metric — workstations, pageviews, active users, followers or employees. Companies license for one year at a time.

rows.t: Each license is sized by its own usage metric: workstations (Print), monthly pageviews (Web), monthly active users (App), combined followers (Social Media), employees (Logo), reach and impressions (Broadcast).
rows.sub: Licenses are bought per weight. Commercial licenses start at $40; prices are in USD.

rows.t: Anyone using the fonts needs a license. When a designer creates something for a client, only the client needs to purchase the licenses; if both use the fonts, both need one.
rows.sub: Freelancers, studios and agencies are independent entities and each need their own license.

rows.t: Since August 2023, licenses for companies run for one year and must then be renewed; longer terms are available at a discount on request. Per the FAQ, licenses for individuals and freelancers have no fixed duration.
rows.sub: The EULA itself states a one-year License Period without distinguishing between companies and individuals.

blocks.title: License Types
blocks.lead: Print, Web, App, Social Media, Logo, and Broadcast are separate licenses — one does not cover another.

rows.t: Installation on a set number of workstations; covers non-embedded material such as print artwork, digital images, apparel and album covers, plus physical products the licensee or its clients sell.
One license per domain or subdomain, capped by monthly pageviews. Also allows embedding in certain electronic documents (PDF, Office), but not the complete character set without written consent.
One license per app or software (mobile, desktop, web app), sized by monthly active users. Video games need a separate Video Game license on request.
A single license for all social profiles where the font appears, sized by combined followers. Required for any commercial use on social media.
Per campaign or broadcast (TV, digital advertising, out-of-home, paid media, digital billboards), limited by reach and estimated impressions. Unlimited coverage available on request.

blocks.title: Additional Costs & Special Cases
blocks.lead: Logos need their own license; outline edits are allowed but the font files themselves are off-limits.

rows.t: One Logo license per company and per distinct logo design (colour and tagline changes excepted), sized by the company’s employee count. The logo may then be used in any context.

Outlines may be edited freely. Modifying the font files directly, renaming the font, or using modified outlines to create a new font is prohibited; third parties may only modify with written authorization.
Partners and collaborators may be given access if the appropriate license is held; the licensee is liable for their compliance. Print shops must delete the fonts after the job.
If usage outgrows the license, Pangram Pangram upgrades it and fully credits what was already paid.
Not addressed in the EULA or FAQ.

blocks.title: Discounts & Trials
blocks.lead: Every font is free to try for personal use — no student or non-profit discount is published.

rows.t: All fonts are free for personal, non-commercial use, including portfolios, client pitches, personal social posts, school projects and dev testing.
rows.sub: Free versions include the complete glyph set but only selected key styles.

rows.t: No student or educational discount is mentioned on the FAQ or in the EULA; school projects are covered by the free personal-use fonts.
Companies can get discounted rates for license durations beyond one year by contacting the foundry.
